title: Finite-subextension tensor models with a common lower bound
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use small pro-etale sites and a coefficient universe containing the set $I_E$ of finite intermediate fields $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_Z=p_Z^*\underline E$, $P_{F,Z}=p_Z^*\underline F$, and $B_Z=p_Z^*\underline\Omega$ for $Z=X,Y$, using the finite-subextension-valued condensed convention [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. View these as section-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], with actual inclusion maps $q_{F,Z}:P_{F,Z}\to B_Z$ and transition maps induced by field inclusions [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories, their standard t-structure, and sheaf tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

The poset $I_E$ is small, nonempty and filtered. The maps $q_{F,Z}$ exhibit $B_Z=\varinjlim_F P_{F,Z}$ in $R_Z$-module sheaves. Each $P_{F,Z}$ is finite free over $R_Z$, and $P_{F,Z}$ and $B_Z$ are flat (tensoring with them is exact). The canonical coefficient identifications make $L=f_R^*$ exact, identify $LP_{F,Y}=P_{F,X}$ and $LB_Y=B_X$, and carry $Lq_{F,Y}$ to $q_{F,X}$.

For every integer $a$ and $C\in D(R_X)^{\ge a}$ there exists a representative $K^\bullet$ with $K^r=0$ for $r<a$. The actual diagram $M_F^\bullet=P_{F,X}\otimes_{R_X}K^\bullet$ represents $P_{F,X}\otimes^L_{R_X}C$, vanishes below the same $a$, and has termwise colimit $B_X\otimes_{R_X}K^\bullet$, representing $B_X\otimes^L_{R_X}C$, with legs $q_{F,X}\otimes1$. For every $A\in D(R_Y)$ and every representative $J^\bullet$ of $A$, the termwise colimit of $P_{F,Y}\otimes_{R_Y}J^\bullet$ is $B_Y\otimes_{R_Y}J^\bullet$ and represents $B_Y\otimes^L_{R_Y}A$. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$ the map induced by the specified legs is an isomorphism
$$\varinjlim_F H^q(P_{F,Y}\otimes^L_{R_Y}A)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(B_Y\otimes^L_{R_Y}A).$$

proof.text: Use the already-stated fieldDiagram and coefficientModules normalization clauses of [lem-sfb-qlbar-internal-hom-coefficient-comparison]. The first supplies filteredness, cofinality of the finite tail, and finite freeness. The second identifies the prescribed complex-defined modules with the regular field modules, retaining every transition and closure leg on sections. Whisker the actual full coefficient cocone by the cofinal tail. The stage and vertex normalizations give an isomorphism to its underlying abelian-sheaf cocone. The faithful module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms and hence reflects this colimit. Thus the prescribed module cocone itself is a colimit. Apply on X and Y.

proof.text: A finite free internal module is a finite biproduct of the regular module, which is the tensor unit. The existing source theorem isDualizable_biproduct_unit shows that this finite biproduct is dualizable, including rank zero. The source theorem ObjectProperty.flat_of_isDualizable makes it flat: tensoring with a dualizable object has a right adjoint as well as a left adjoint. Transfer this assertion to the section-ring tensor via [lem-c2-internal-section-module-flatness] and along the finite-free isomorphisms of step 1.

proof.text: Prove closure flatness directly for the filtered category AsSmall (Under E). Filtered colimits of module sheaves are exact, transferred through the faithful exact forgetful functor to abelian sheaves. Tensor preserves the coefficient colimit in each variable. Consequently tensorLeft of its vertex is naturally isomorphic to the composite of the functor sending a module to its diagram of stage tensors and the filtered colimit functor. Both preserve finite limits: the former pointwise by stage flatness, the latter by exactness. Symmetry gives the right tensor assertion, and tensor preserves finite colimits as a left adjoint. Transport through siteSheafTensorRightIso to obtain precisely IsFlatOnSite.

Use [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] and the actual coefficient-change naturality square. In internal module objects, inverse image of the regular F module restricted along E to F identifies with the regular F module on X restricted along the corresponding inclusion. The underlying isomorphism is alpha_F. Its linearity is the coefficient square and multiplicativity of alpha_F. Naturality of these isomorphisms follows from that same square for F to G. Transfer the resulting natural isomorphism through the fixed section equivalences, using the normalization equations in coefficientModules. Pullback preserves the coefficient colimit, so uniqueness of colimit vertices gives the closure isomorphism with the required equality of every cocone leg. Exactness of pullback and the asserted alpha squares are the existing Cartesian instances.

proof.text: For an arbitrary representative K of A, choose one flat-term K-flat resolution p:V to K using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Apply the right-fixed comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] to V. It is natural in every first complex, and its value on P[0] compares the total tensor of P[0] and V with derivedTensor(P[0],QV). The canonical single-factor totalization isomorphism identifies that total tensor with the degreewise tensor P tensor V. This single-factor isomorphism is also natural in P; check the inverse on the degree-(0,n) total summand. For flat P, the exact functor P tensor - preserves the quasi-isomorphism p. Invert its image under Q and compose with the fixed comparison and QV isomorphic to A. Naturality in P follows from the natural square P tensor p and the fixed comparison. Apply to all finite stages and the flat closure vertex, obtaining the specified transition and cocone equations simultaneously, for every possibly unbounded K.

proof.text: For a fixed term $T^r$, [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], and the symmetry $s\otimes t\mapsto t\otimes s$ of the sheafified tensor, carry the module colimit in step 1 to the colimit with vertex $B_Z\otimes_{R_Z}T^r$ and legs $q_{F,Z}\otimes1_{T^r}$. The transition maps are $a_{F,G}\otimes1_{T^r}$. They commute with the differential: $(a_{F,G}\otimes1)(1\otimes d_T)=(1\otimes d_T)(a_{F,G}\otimes1)$, both sending $s\otimes t$ to $a_{F,G}(s)\otimes d_T(t)$, and the identical calculation holds with $q_F$. Hence the termwise colimit complex is exactly $(B_Z\otimes T^r,1\otimes d_T^r)_r$, with the asserted legs. Take $T=K$ on $X$ and $T=J$ on $Y$. Since tensor with the zero sheaf is zero, every $P_{F,X}\otimes K$ and their colimit vanish in all degrees $r<a$, with the same $a$ independently of $F$. Step 6 identifies these actual diagrams with the derived scalar-extension diagrams.

source.place: Tag 03EP, lemma-tensor-commute-colimits (2), applied in each cochain degree

proof.text: The degreewise cocone of step 7 is a colimit of complexes, since evaluation functors jointly detect colimits. Filtered colimits of module sheaves are exact by transfer through the exact faithful colimit-preserving forgetful functor to abelian sheaves. The already-proved source result [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] therefore shows that ordinary complex homology preserves this cocone colimit. Transport this IsColimit witness along DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors, the natural isomorphism Q followed by derived homology with ordinary complex homology. This transport retains the specified legs, so it proves the exact homology-cocone assertion for each q and every unbounded representative.
